[QUERENT] "machine-mediated research"

[ANSWER]

Machine-mediated research is a process where AI tools, large language models (LLMs), and automated agents gather, analyze, synthesize, and present information or scientific data on behalf of humans.

Key Aspects

• B2B and Commercial Buying: Buyers increasingly start their research using AI chatbots (such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Bing Copilot) and answer engines rather than traditional search engine lists. This makes "citation architecture" and brand visibility inside AI-generated shortlists critical for marketing and sales.
• Scientific and Academic Work: AI tools (such as Consensus, Elicit, and Semantic Scholar) accelerate literature reviews, clinical trial data analysis, and pattern identification. However, challenges remain regarding relational fidelity—where models might retrieve correct facts but misassign the underlying scientific connections or edges.
• Dual-Layer Literature: Emerging frameworks propose separating machine-reception layers (AI-generated proofs and training-layer artifacts) from human-interpretation layers (contextualized peer review and summaries).
• Legal and Governance Context: Courts (such as the Delhi High Court in ANI v. OpenAI) have begun evaluating machine-mediated research and AI training workflows under a technologically neutral approach to copyright.
